parole.testo: From the Proto-Uralic *sᴕ̈ third-person personal pronoun of the ancestor language after it was appended to the word of possession. According to some linguists this attachment happened in the Proto-Uralic era, while others think it happened much later when the Hungarian language became independent.

parole.significato: Appended to a noun to form a diminutive noun. No longer productive.
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Uralic *-tś.
Inherited from Proto-Uralic *-j.

parole.significato: Added to a noun, an adjective, a verb or less frequently to an adverb to form a verb.
parole.testo: From a Proto-Uralic *-l suffix.
Possibly from Proto-Uralic *mᴕ̈ (“I”); see also én (“I”). Cognate with Northern Mansi -м (-m, “my”).

parole.significato: Added to a verb (or rarely to a noun) to form a noun. No longer productive in this sense.
parole.testo: It can be traced back to the Proto-Uralic *-m.
From Proto-Uralic *nä (“this”) + Proto-Uralic *-k or Proto-Uralic *-ŋ (“lative suffix”). Compare Proto-Finnic *-k (“forming lative adverbs”).

From Proto-Uralic *roγ- (“nearness”) or Proto-Ugric *raŋɜ (“surface”) + -l (archaic ablative case suffix) formed the suffixed nominal *roγol. This turned into a postposition during the ancient Hungarian era. The γ inside the word was dropped and the shortened ról lost its independent role and became

parole.significato: Added to a noun to form an adjective meaning "having something, a quality"; sometimes referred to as ornative.
parole.testo: Presumably can be traced back to a Proto-Uralic *-ć suffix.

parole.significato: Forms the accusative case for nouns, adjectives, pronouns and numerals.
parole.testo: First attested in the end of 12th century. Of debated origin. According to the most accepted theory, it is from a possessive suffix that originated either from a *t-initial demonstrative pronoun or from the Proto-Uralic *tᴕ̈ (“you”) personal pronoun.

parole.significato: past-tense and past-participle suffix (homonymous form in the vast majority of verbs):
parole.testo: * Past-participle suffix: From Proto-Uralic *-tt. First attested in 1055. * Past-tense suffix: From the past-participle suffix. First attested in the end of 12th century.

parole.significato: Added to a verb to form a noun.
parole.testo: First attested in 1055. From Proto-Uralic *-tt.

parole.significato: A causative (e.g. kelt, teremt) or instantaneous (e.g. ért, tilt) suffix for verbs.
parole.testo: First attested in the end of 12th century. From Proto-Uralic *-tt.

parole.significato: -less, un-, dis- (a privative suffix added to a noun or an adjective to form adjectives with a meaning of lacking somet…
parole.testo: From the Proto-Uralic *-tt (privative suffix) + *-l (nominal suffix), then in the Ancient Hungarian era the -n (adverbial suffix) was added.

parole.significato: past-tense and past-participle suffix (homonymous form in the vast majority of verbs):
parole.testo: * Past-participle suffix: From Proto-Uralic *-tt. First attested in 1055. * Past-tense suffix: From the past-participle suffix. First attested in the end of 12th century.

parole.significato: Forms the first-person plural present tense of verbs (indicative mood, indefinite conjugation).
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *-mVk (“our one possession”) or Proto-Uralic *-n-mVk (“our multiple possessions”). Cognate with Moksha -нк (-nk, “our one or multiple possessions”).

Of disputed origin: * According to the traditional view, developed from Proto-Uralic *wäke (“strength, force”), extended with -l (“obsolete ablative suffix”) * According to a newer view, from Proto-Uralic *pälä (“half, side”). Cognate with Northern Mansi -ыл (-yl).

parole.significato: Added to a noun to form a verb. Less frequently, it can also be found added onto other parts of speech.
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *-ta-. The preceding vowel, if any, is from the original stem of the root word.

parole.significato: Used to form the lative, expressing the direction (“where to”) or the purpose (“what for”).
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *-j, which served as part of a diphthong (together with the vowel at the end of the noun stem) and became -á/-é.

parole.significato: to give or shift (something) to or near someone or somewhere
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Uralic *ëmta-. Cognates include Finnish antaa and Estonian andma.
From Proto-Uralic *soŋkɜ (“old, to grow old”).
From Proto-Uralic *aŋe.

parole.significato: lip (either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth)
parole.testo: From the obsolete aj (“valley; opening”) + -k (diminutive suffix), from Proto-Uralic *aŋe (“opening, incision, deepening”). Alternatively, possible cognate of Yakut айах (ayax, “mouth”).

From Proto-Uralic *ëla (“space, area under something, under(neath), the lower (part)”). (Spelled *ala in Uralonet.) Originally it was a noun; today it is used in compound words, see al-. Cognate with Finnish ala, ala-, Erzya ало (alo).
From Proto-Uralic *ëla. Cognates include Finnish ala-.
Lexicalization of al (“lower part”) + -tt (locative suffix). The root al- is from Proto-Uralic *ëla.

From the obsolete alk (“conformity, adaptation, adjustment to something”) + -alom (noun-forming suffix). The original stem is probably related to Hungarian alkot (“to create”) and alku (“deal”), and it may also be related to Hungarian olt (“to vaccinate”), which may derive from Proto-Uralic *alɜ- (“

parole.significato: to create (especially something creative, imaginative, and originative)
parole.testo: From the same alk- stem as alkuszik (“to bargain”) + -t (instantaneous suffix). The original stem is probably related to Hungarian alkalom (“opportunity”) and alku (“deal”), and it may also be related to Hungarian olt (“to vaccinate”), which may derive from Proto-Uralic *alɜ- (“to add/fasten to some
Probably from Proto-Uralic *ańa (“wife of an older male relative; mother”).

Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *attɜ (“father, grandfather”) + -a (diminutive suffix or possessive suffix). It is also possible that it originates from infant talk. Cognates include Erzya атя (aťa) and Udmurt атай (ataj).

parole.significato: to become obsolete / dated / outmoded (to continuously go out of style and fashion)
parole.testo: From avik (“to become old or obsolete”) + -ul (verb-forming suffix)., from Proto-Uralic *soŋkɜ (“old, to grow old”). Related to agg and avar, via the same Uralic root.

parole.significato: the (for words beginning with a vowel)
parole.testo: The pronoun and determiner senses probably derive from an earlier a + a pronoun-forming suffix -z, where the former element originates from Proto-Uralic *o or *u (“that, that other”). Its cognates include Moksha омба (omba, “other”), омбоце (omboce, “second”), Eastern Mari умбал (umbal, “far, distan

From Old Hungarian bolo (almost certainly *boló), from Proto-Uralic *pola. Cognates include Southern Mansi po̰l, Northern Mansi пил (pil), Komi-Zyrian пул (pul, “cowberry”), Finnish puola (“cowberry”). The dialectal variants indicate the sound change *l > ʎ > j > gy.

parole.significato: skin (outer protective layer of the body of any animal, including of a human)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *pere.

parole.significato: to trickle, dribble, run, flow, stream (to flow in a very thin stream or drop continuously)
parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Uralic *ćorɜ- (“drip, flow, ooze”) + -og (frequentative verb-forming suffix). This, however, is uncertain due to the onomatopoeic nature of the word. Cognates include Northern Mansi соргуӈкве (sorguňkve, “to stream, to flow”), Eastern Khanty ᲊө̆рәӽԓәта (tjø̆rəḥłəta, “to flow”) an

parole.significato: to shut, close (without using a key and a lock, only with a handle)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *čukka- (“to lock up, hide”).
Uncertain. Maybe from Proto-Uralic *tora- (“strife; struggle, battle”) + -gál (frequentative suffix), in which case related to Finnish torua, Erzya тюремс (ťurems).

parole.significato: to stick, tuck, insert, push in (into something: -ba/-be)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *tuŋke-. Cognate with Finnish tunkea, Erzya тонгомс (tongoms).
From Proto-Uralic *e-. Cognates include Finnish että and Estonian et.

Native development but its origin is disputed: # Lexicalization of e/ez (“this”) demonstrative pronoun (ultimately from Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”)) + -l (ablative case suffix) which changed to gy via palatalization and affrication. # Derivation from e/ez (“this”) demonstrative pronoun (ultimately fro

parole.significato: mouse (any mammal of the rodent family Muridae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *šiŋere. Cognates include Northern Mansi таӈкыр (taňkyr), Erzya чеерь (čejeŕ), Finnish hiiri and Estonian hiir. The hardware sense is a semantic loan from English mouse.
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *älɜ- (“to raise, carry”). Cognates include Northern Mansi а̄лмуӈкве (ālmuňkve, “lift”).
From Proto-Uralic *ime- (“to suck”) + -ik. Cognate with Finnish imeä.
eml (“to nurse, breast-feed”) + -ő (present-participle suffix). From the same Proto-Uralic *ime- stem as emik + -l.
The em- stem is from Proto-Uralic *emä (“mother, woman”). The -s- is a diminutive suffix.

parole.significato: bile (a bitter brownish-yellow or greenish-yellow secretion produced by the liver, stored in the gall bladder, and disc…
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *säppä. Cognates include Finnish sappi, Estonian sapp and Erzya сэпе (sëpe). Its current form is the result of rebracketing an earlier form *ep possessive-suffixed with -e, compare vese, zúza, ipa, and possibly apa.

parole.significato: in the evening (from approximately 6 p.m. until going to bed; depends on working hours, daylight length, etc.)
parole.testo: The adverb sense is from the former est (“evening”) + -vel (“with”) (a derivation similar to reggel or tavasszal). First the final -l wore off and the adverb estve (“in the evening”) was used for a long time (still in use today in dialects), later the -v was dropped. The noun sense became independen
From Proto-Uralic *sewe- (“to eat”) + -ik. Cognates include Northern Mansi тэ̄ӈкве (tè̄ňkve), Finnish syödä and Estonian sööma.

parole.significato: this, it (used as a pronoun, that is, instead of a noun phrase)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”). Cognates include Finnish että, Estonian et, Erzya эте (ete).
From Proto-Uralic *puwe. Cognates include Finnish puu.

parole.significato: privet (any of various shrubs and small trees in the genus Ligustrum)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *pajiw. Cognate with Finnish paju and Estonian paju.

parole.significato: to devour, gorge, wolf, scarf (eat greedily, voraciously, or ravenously)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *pala- (“to devour”). Cognates include Finnish palaa (“to burn”).
Inherited from Proto-Uralic *ponče (“tail”). Older hypotheses have attempted to derive far from Proto-Uralic *pure- (“back, rear”) or Proto-Finno-Ugric *perä (“back, rear”).

From Proto-Uralic *parɜ- (“to cut, scrape, groove”) + -g (frequentative suffix). Related to Northern Mansi поруӈкве (poruňkve, “to hollow out”), Northern Selkup пуртыӄа (purtyqa, “to drill, to perforate”) and Kamassian пааргǝ (paargǝ, “to cut”).

From Proto-Uralic *päŋe, by rebracketing of the possessive form feje into fej + e instead of earlier fe + je. Cognates include Southern Mansi пӧӈ (pöň), Northern Mansi пуӈк (puňk), Finnish pää, Estonian pea and Erzya пе (pe). Compare fő.

Of debated origin: # From an unattested fejsz (“to cut, separate”) + -e (obsolete present-participle suffix). # From Proto-Uralic *pᴕ̈jćɜ, with a Hungarian nominal-forming suffix or perhaps a diminutive suffix.

parole.significato: up, upward, upwards (to a physically higher or more elevated position)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *pide.
From Proto-Uralic *pᴕnɜ (“fart; let out a fart”) + -g.

From Old Hungarian fioɣ or fió with the original stem fi akin to Proto-Uralic *pojka (“son, boy”) + -ú (“archaic diminutive suffix”) (also attested as -oɣ, -ó in Old Hungarian). Cognates include Northern Mansi пыг (pyg, “son, boy”), Udmurt пи (pi, “son, boy”), Komi-Zyrian пи (pi, “son, boy”), Erzya
From Proto-Uralic *piŋe. Cognates include Northern Mansi пуӈк (puňk), Erzya пей (pej), Finnish pii.
From Proto-Uralic *püŋe.

parole.significato: to spin (to make thread by twisting fibers)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *puna-. Cognates include Southern Mansi po̰n-, Erzya понамс (ponams) and Finnish punoa.
First attested in 1372. Of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *pürke- (*pᴕrγɜ) (“to turn, revolve, spin”) + -dul (reflexive suffix).

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; perhaps; modello unc/uncertain
parole.significato: to turn (change the direction or orientation of something)
parole.testo: First attested in 1372. Of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *pürke- (*pᴕrγɜ-) (“to turn, revolve, spin”) + -dít (causative suffix).

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; perhaps; modello unc/uncertain
parole.testo: Of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *pürke- (“to turn, revolve, spin”) + -gat (frequentative suffix). First attested in c. 1395.
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *pürke- (“to turn, revolve, spin”) + -og (frequentative suffix).

parole.significato: to run (to move forward quickly on the feet)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *pukta- (“to caper, jump, run”).

parole.significato: to fear, to be afraid of something (-tól/-től)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *pele-. Cognates include Northern Mansi [script needed] (pil-), Erzya пелемс (pelems) and Finnish pelätä.
From Proto-Uralic *pälä. Cognates include Northern Mansi па̄л (pāl, “half, side”), Udmurt пал (pal, “half, side”), Erzya [script needed] (peĺ), [script needed] (peĺe, “half, side”).

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; perhaps; modello unc/uncertain
parole.testo: Of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *päjwä + -ny (noun-forming suffix).
From Proto-Uralic *pesä. Cognates include Finnish pesä and Estonian pesa. With nominal-forming suffix -k (compare ének, lélek etc.).
From Proto-Uralic *puwa- (“to blow”). Of the same origin as fú.
Of debated origin: # From Proto-Uralic *pura- (“to bore; drill”). # Native word from fúl (“to stab”).

parole.significato: to boil, to cook (normally in water, as opposed to oil)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *peje- (“to boil, cook”). Cognates include Erzya and Moksha пиемс (pijems, “to boil”).
From Proto-Uralic *kompa. Cognates include Northern Mansi хумп (hump) and Finnish kummuta.
From Proto-Uralic *kaďa-.
From Proto-Uralic *kojwa (“birch”), alternately reconstructed as *koxjï. Compare Finnish koivu, Nganasan [script needed] (kụa), Eastern Mari куэ (kue), and Moksha келу (kelu).
From Proto-Uralic *kala. Cognates include Northern Khanty хўԓ (hŭł), Northern Mansi хӯл (hūl), Erzya and Moksha кал (kal), Finnish and Estonian kala.

parole.significato: to die (to stop living; to become dead)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kale-. Cognates include Northern Mansi хо̄луӈкве (hōluňkve), Finnish kuolla, Erzya and Moksha куломс (kuloms).

parole.significato: to proceed, progress, advance (to move, pass, or go forward or onward)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kulke-. Cognates include Finnish kulkea (“to go”).

parole.significato: to postpone, defer, delay (followed by -ra/-re) (to put off the completion of something until a later time)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kulke- (“be on the move, move (to land, water)”) + -aszt (causative verb-forming suffix). Cognates include Finnish kulkea.

parole.significato: to hear (to perceive sounds through the ear)
parole.testo: From the conflation of Proto-Uralic *kontale- (compare Old Hungarian hadl (“hear”), Northern Mansi хӯнтлуӈкве (hūntluňkve), Finnish kuunnella) and Proto-Uralic *kuwle- (compare Northern Mansi хӯлуӈкве (hūluňkve) and Finnish kuulla).

parole.significato: to keep postponing, keep putting off
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kulke- (“be on the move, move (to land, water)”) + -ogat (“frequentative verb-forming suffix”).
From Proto-Uralic *kuńśe.
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *kura (“hoar frost, fine snow”) + -at (noun-forming suffix). Cognates include Finnish kuura.

Back-formation from haránték, harántos (“thwart”), two obsolete adjectives, themselves from Proto-Uralic *kura (“curved, skewed, crooked; make curved, skewed, crooked”), related to Udmurt кырыж (kyryž, “crooked, curved, bent”) and Tundra Nenets хара (xara, “bend, curve, turn”). Created during the Hu

parole.significato: advantage, benefit, use, point (that which makes something meaningful)
parole.testo: Uncertain, perhaps a Hungarian derivation from a proto-language. However, its cognates are debated: # From Proto-Uralic *kaća- (“gift; to present a gift”). # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *kaswa- (“to grow, increase”). Compare Finnish kasvaa.
From Proto-Uralic *kutte. Cognates include Finnish kuusi, Northern Mansi хо̄т (hōt), Northern Khanty хәт (hət).

parole.significato: to get, arrive at, pass, progress towards (a certain location)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kattɜ- (“to penetrate, go ahead, move somewhere”). Cognates include Northern Khanty хӑтты (hătty, “to move, to travel”). The suffix -hat/-het originated from this verb. First attested in c. 1372.

Cognate with Northern Mansi хо̄тпан (hōtpan, “60”). From the numeral hat (“six”) + van where van cannot be attested as an independent word (it is not the verb van). Compare also nyolcvan (“80”) as well as negyven (“40”), ötven (“50”), hetven (“70”), and kilencven (“90”). The second element might be

Disputed, possibly from Proto-Uralic. Two different comparisons have been proposed, both with their own problems: * Akin to Proto-Samoyedic *koəjə (“mountain”). * Akin to Proto-Finnic *kaca (“point”), Proto-Samic *keaćē (“point”). Abondolo (1992) considers the latter comparison "slightly less unconv

parole.significato: testicle, testis (the male sex and endocrine gland)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kojera (“male animal”). Cognates include Northern Mansi ха̄р (hār).
From Proto-Uralic *kuńćɜ, from *ku (“interrogative stem”). Cognates include Komi-Zyrian кыдз (kydź, “how”), Eastern Mari кузе (kuze, “how”), perhaps Finnish konsa (“when”).
From Proto-Uralic *kuŋe. Cognates include Hungarian hó (“month”), Finnish and Estonian kuu.
From Proto-Uralic *kule.

From otherwise unattested *hol (“morning, dawn”) + nap (“day”). Originally meant "morning". For the "morning" > "tomorrow" development, compare German Morgen (“morning”), morgen (“tomorrow”) or Spanish mañana (“morning”), mañana (“tomorrow”). The prefix is from the Proto-Uralic *kude (“morning”).

From Old Hungarian hoszjú or hozu (*hosszú), from Proto-Uralic *koćɜ; cognates include Komi-Zyrian кузь (kuź, “long”) and Northern Mansi хоса (hosa /⁠χosa⁠/, “long”). Erzya кувака (kuvaka, “long”) and Moksha кувака (kuvaka, “long”) probably derive from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kawka (“long”), which has no
From Proto-Uralic *kuńa-. Cognates include Northern Mansi хонюӈкве (honûňkve, “blink”).

parole.significato: to peel (to come off in layers)
parole.testo: First attested in 1527. From Proto-Uralic *kama (“skin”) + -lik. Cognates include Finnish kamara.

parole.significato: to peel (to remove the skin or outer covering of)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kama (“skin”) + -oz (verb-forming suffix). First attested in c. 1416. Cognates include Finnish kamara.
Native word, probably from Proto-Uralic.

parole.significato: to hurl, spout, fling, throw, toss (especially a shapeless, disorderly amount with many small components or pieces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kanɜ- (“to strew, pour, throw, dig”).cognates include Northern Mansi хӯнуӈкве (hūnuňkve, “to scoop out fish from a barrel”)
Of disputed origin. Either from Proto-Uralic *końćkɜ (“bast, bark”) (whence Finnish koskut), or related to hasad. First attested in 1086.
Probably from Proto-Uralic *kurɜ (“curved, skewed, crooked”) + -ít (causative verb-forming suffix).
From Proto-Uralic *kutte (“ridge”).

parole.significato: male (chiefly an animal of the male sex)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kojema (“man, human”), derived from *koje. Cognates include Northern Mansi хум (hum, “man, male”).

parole.significato: to call (to request, summon, or beckon)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *kaŋe- (“to call”).
From Proto-Uralic *kume. Cognates include Tundra Nenets хавˮ (xaw, “fragile snow”), possibly Omok ку (ku, “snow”).
From Proto-Uralic *kuŋe. Cognates include Hungarian hold (“moon”), Finnish and Estonian kuu.
From Proto-Uralic *kone. Cognates include Northern Mansi ханул (hanul), Finnish kainalo and Estonian kaenal.
From Old Hungarian helgy, from Proto-Uralic *käďwä.
From Proto-Uralic *kuńśe (“urine”).
From Proto-Uralic *kuńśe (“star”).

Probably from Proto-Uralic *kaća (“young unmarried man”). Originally meant "young", the sense of "main protagonist" developed during the Hungarian language reform taking place in the 18th-19th centuries. Cognates include Northern Mansi хӯсь (hūsʹ, “servant, jack”).

From Proto-Uralic *jänte: /jænte/ → /ide/ as a phonological shift, plus a final /-ɡ/ as a noun-forming suffix. For the jV → i shift, compare iszik; for the nt → d shift, compare fed or köd; for the final g, compare kéreg or réteg. Cognates include Northern Mansi я̄нтэв (â̄ntèv, “bowstring”) and Finn

parole.significato: to set off, set out, head somewhere (begin a trip)
parole.testo: The stem is likely from Proto-Uralic *jome- (“to go, to set off”) + -dul (verb-forming suffix).

parole.significato: to start, launch, set off, get underway, set in motion
parole.testo: The stem is likely from Proto-Uralic *jome- (“to go, to set off”) + -dít.
From Proto-Uralic *ëppe (“father-in-law”).

parole.significato: mercy (relenting; forbearance to cause or allow harm to another)
parole.testo: Of uncertain origin, perhaps from Proto-Uralic *jȣrɜ (“to get lost”) + -alom (noun-forming suffix).

parole.significato: to exterminate, to extirpate, to eradicate, to slaughter, to destroy
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *šure-.

parole.significato: to drink (to consume through the mouth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *jëxe- (“to drink, imbibe”) + -ik. Cognates include Northern Mansi аюӈкве (aûňkve), Finnish juoda and Estonian jooma.
From Proto-Uralic *jälke (“trace”). Cognates include Finnish jälki and Estonian jälg.
From Proto-Uralic *jäŋe. Cognates include Northern Mansi я̄ӈк (â̄ňk), Eastern Khanty йӛӈк (jjəṇk), Erzya эй (ej), Estonian jää and Finnish jää.

parole.significato: river (occurs in compound proper names, such as Sajó, Berettyó, Héjő)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *joke. Cognates include Northern Mansi я̄ (â̄, “river”), Finnish joki (“river”), Estonian jõgi (“river”), Karelian jogi (“river”), Veps jogi (“river”). Replaced by folyó.
From Proto-Uralic *jᴕ̈ɣɜ-. Cognates include Northern Mansi йиӈкве (jiňkve, “to come, to become”) and Eastern Khanty йө̆вәтта (jø̆wətta, “to come, to arrive”).
From Proto-Uralic *kämä + -ny (nominal-forming suffix). Cognates include Erzya кеме (keme, “hard”). For the suffix, compare sovány (“thin”).

parole.significato: two (mostly used in place of a whole noun phrase or as a predicate, but not usually as a counter before nouns)
parole.testo: From két. The suffix may reflect Proto-Uralic *-k, being the only trace thereof in Hungarian.

parole.significato: few, little (not as many/much as usual or as expected)
parole.testo: Possibly derived from Proto-Uralic *kepä (“light (weight)”); compare with Estonian kebja (“easy, quick”), Finnish kepeä (“light (weight), easy, quick”), and Northern Sami geahpas (“light”).

parole.significato: who (what person or people; which person or people)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *ke, the same root from which the Finnish ken and Ter Sami kie are derived.
From Proto-Uralic *kečɜ. Cognates include Northern Mansi касай (kasaj).
From Proto-Uralic *käktä.

parole.significato: hand (the part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in a human)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *käte. Cognates include Southern Mansi кӓт (kät), Northern Mansi ка̄т (kāt), Moksha кядь (käď), Erzya кедь (keď), Eastern Mari кид (kid), Finnish käsi and Estonian käsi (“hand”).
From Proto-Uralic *kije. Cognate with Finnish kyy (“viper”), Moksha куй (kuj, “snake”) and Udmurt кый (kyj, “snake”).
From Proto-Uralic *künte.
From Proto-Uralic *küńele. Cognates include Finnish kyynel.
From Proto-Uralic *künče.

parole.significato: to bind, tie (to attach or fasten with string)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *kütke- (“to bind”). Cognates include Finnish kytkeä.
From Proto-Uralic *kiwe. Cognate with Southern Mansi кӱ (kü), кӱв (küv), Northern Mansi кав (kav), Erzya кев (kev), Finnish kivi, Estonian kivi.

parole.significato: sheet (thin, flat piece of any solid material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *lappɜ (“flat surface”), either directly or as a back-formation from lapos.
From Proto-Uralic *lappɜ (“flat surface”) + -os (adjective-forming suffix). Cognate to Finnish lape, Erzya лапужа (lapuža).
From Proto-Uralic *lappɜ (“surface, flat”) + -ít (verb-forming suffix).

From Proto-Uralic *lᴕ̈ppɜ (“butterfly”). Cognates include Southern Mansi лӓпӓх (läpäh), Northern Mansi ла̄панты (lāpanty, “butterfly”) (Sosva), Livvi liipoi (“butterfly”), and Eastern Mari лыве (lyve, “butterfly”).

parole.motivo_incerta: Of uncertain origin; perhaps; modello unc/uncertain
parole.testo: Of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *lowkke (“hole, opening, cavity, hollow”).

parole.significato: leg (of a human or an animal)
parole.testo: Possibly from Proto-Uralic *luwe (“bone”) + the suffix -b, used in an unusual diminutive function. Compare Northern Mansi лу (lu), Erzya ловажа (lovaža) and Finnish luu. For a similar semantic evolution, from "bone" to "leg", compare that of German Bein. Alternately, from Proto-Uralic *lümpe (“blade

parole.significato: moor (region with poor, marshy soil, peat, and heath)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *lappa (“floating log”).

parole.significato: to see (to perceive with the eyes)
parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Uralic *lᴕttɜ- (“to see”), related to Tundra Nenets лэтбась (letbasʹ°), лэтрамбась (letrambasʹ°, “to guard, to protect, to watch over”). As a prefix in compound words, it's a calque of German Schau or Seh(en).
From Proto-Uralic *läme. Cognate with Finnish liemi.

parole.significato: leak (an opening on a ship's hull where water can enter)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *lekka- (“gap, tear, crack; to cut, cleave”). Compare Finnish leikata and Tundra Nenets лекабтамбась (lyekabtambasʹ°), лекабтась (lyekabtasʹ°, “to crack, to split, to cleave”).
From Proto-Uralic *läppe (“spleen”).

parole.significato: to bite (of animals, chiefly snakes, sometimes dogs or chinches; used either with -t/-ot/-at/-et/-öt or with -ba/-be)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Uralic *mura-, (*murɜ) (“bit, crumb; crumble, crack”).

parole.significato: to stay, remain (to remain in a particular place; to stay behind while others withdraw; to be left after others have be…
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *mᴕrɜ- (“to restrain”) + -ad (frequentative suffix). Related to Tundra Nenets марпась (marpasʹ°), марць (marcʹ°, “to grab, to grasp”).

parole.significato: to go, travel (whether on foot or by any vehicle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *mene-. Cognates include Northern Mansi минуӈкве (minuňkve), Finnish mennä and Estonian minna.
From Proto-Uralic *mińä. Cognate with Northern Mansi мань (manʹ) and Finnish miniä.
From Proto-Uralic *me.
From Proto-Uralic *mi.

Derived from the obsolete mony (“egg”), which originates from Proto-Uralic *muna (“egg; testicles”). Or from Proto-Turkic *bōńurï, compare Chuvash мӑйӑр (măjăr, “hazelnut”), Yakut моонньоҕон (moonńoɣon, “black currants”).
From Proto-Uralic *mᴕnɜ- (*monɜ-) + -d (frequentative suffix).
From Proto-Uralic *muna. Cognates include Northern Mansi мӯӈи (mūňi) and Finnish muna.

parole.significato: to wash something (to clean with water, including brushing one’s teeth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *mośke-.
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *mᴕńće- or *mᴕćɜ- (“to move”) + -og (verb-forming suffix).

parole.significato: liver (a large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *mëksa, by rebracketing of the possessive form mája into máj + a instead of the earlier má + ja. Cognates include Northern Mansi ма̄йт (mājt), Finnish maksa and Estonian maks.
From Proto-Uralic *mete, borrowed from Proto-Tocharian *ḿətə, in turn from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu. Finno-Ugric cognates include Finnish mesi and Estonian mesi.

parole.significato: neck (the part of the body connecting the head and the trunk found in humans and some animals)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *ńᴕkkɜ (“neck”).
From Proto-Uralic *ńale-. Cognates include Finnish nuolla.
From Proto-Uralic *ńäle-. Cognates include Finnish niellä.
From Proto-Uralic *nᴕje- + -t (causative suffix).
From Proto-Uralic *ńukśe.

parole.significato: poplar (any of various deciduous trees of the genus Populus, including aspen and cottonwood)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *ńore (“marsh”).

parole.significato: handle (the part of an object which is designed to be held in the hand when used or moved)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *nüde. Cognates include Finnish nysi, Northern Mansi нал (nal), Erzya недь (neď).
From Proto-Uralic *ńële. Cognates include Southern Mansi ńėl, Northern Mansi ня̄л (nâ̄l), Finnish nuoli, Estonian nool.
From Proto-Uralic *nᴕje- (whence also nyit (“to open”)) + -lik (reflexive suffix). First attested after 1416.
From Proto-Uralic *ńomala. Cognates include Northern Sami njoammil, Tundra Enets наба (naba, “hare”) and Erzya нумоло (numolo, “hare”).
From Proto-Uralic *ńiwŋɜ or *ńiŋe (“maggot, worm”). Cognates include Northern Mansi ниӈк (niňk).

parole.significato: to wear away, to wear out
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *ńüke- (“to rip, tear”). Cognates include Northern Mansi няви (nâvi) and Finnish nykiä.

From Proto-Uralic *nime. Cognates include Southern Mansi näm, Northern Mansi нам (nam), Finnish nimi and Estonian nimi. The Uralic word may be a cognate of Proto-Indo-European *h₁nómn̥, or a variety of other similar words found throughout Eurasian languages.
From Proto-Uralic *niŋä (“woman”). Cognates include Northern Mansi нэ̄ (nè̄) and Erzya ни (ni).
From the same Proto-Uralic *omte as odú + -r (obsolete diminutive suffix).
From Proto-Uralic *aŋa- (“to loosen, open (up), untie”) + -d (frequentative suffix). Cognates include Finnish avata.
From Proto-Uralic *luke- + -s (obsolete frequentative verb-forming suffix). For the -s suffix, compare keres (“to search”).
From or (“peak; a variant form of orr (“nose”)”) + -m (noun-forming suffix), from Proto-Uralic *wëre (“mountain”).
From Proto-Uralic *we̮ri, *wara, *wōri, *wëre (“mountain”). Cognates include Finnish vuori.

Uncertain. Perhaps from a Proto-Uralic *porɜ (“dust, sand”), but the absence of the expected sound change *p > *f is hard to explain. Compare with Finnish poro (“burning ash, coarse dust, debris”) and Northern Mansi порс (pors, “garbage, waste, dust”).
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *ruŋke- (“to chew”). Cognates include Tundra Nenets лунггбась (lunggbasʹ°, “to gnaw”).
From Proto-Uralic *raćɜ (“hole”). Cognates include Komi-Zyrian розь (roź, “opening, hole”).
From Proto-Uralic *repäć + -ka (diminutive suffix) Cognates include Finnish repo and Komi-Permyak руч (ruć). Doublet of ravasz. The slang sense is probably a back-formation from rókázik (“to vomit”).
Probably from Proto-Uralic *śaŋke (“taste, smell; have a smell, smell, taste good”).

parole.significato: ribbon, tape, band, sash, stripe, strip
parole.testo: Controversial origin: * From Proto-Uralic *śale- (“knit”). * From szál + -ag.

parole.significato: eye (visual organ in humans and animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *śilmä, then from szimi, via szüm in one dialect (such as the one used in the Old Hungarian Lamentations of Mary), resulting in dialectal szöm, as well as via szëm and the current, standard szem from another dialect.

From the same stem as the verb szeret (“to love”) + -elem (noun-forming suffix). The stem szer comes from the verbal application of Proto-Uralic *śerɜ (“row, order”) noun with the meaning ‘to join; to be linked / related to each other’.

From the same stem as the noun szerelem (“romantic love”) + -et (momentane verb-forming suffix). The stem szer comes from the verbal application of Proto-Uralic *śerɜ (“row, order”) nounverb with the meaning ‘to join; to be linked / related to each other’.

parole.significato: aperture, mouth, entrance, opening, orifice (of a hollow object or natural formation, e.g. of a mine, a cave, a pot, a…
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *ćunti (“mouth, throat”)

From the same Proto-Uralic root *śoxi (“mouth”) or *śuwe (“mouth”) as Finnish suu and Estonian suu. Rebracketing of the possessive form szája into száj + a instead of earlier szá + ja, while it usually retains the original, shorter stem in 1st- and 2nd-person possessive forms (see the tables below).

parole.significato: thread (a long, thin and flexible form of material, generally with a round cross-section, used in sewing, weaving or in…
parole.testo: Of debated origin: # Most likely from Proto-Uralic *śale (“gut, intestine”) (for sematic parallels, cf. Proto-Germanic *garnō (“intestines, gut”) → Proto-Germanic *garną (“yarn”), Proto-Germanic *langô (“rectum”) → Proto-Finnic *lanka (“yarn, thread”)). # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *śëlkaw (“pole, rod,

Of controversial origin: * From Proto-Uralic *śᴕwɜ. * From Proto-Finno-Ugric *śuka (“bark; skin”). Related to Northern Mansi сов (sov, “leather, skin, hide of an animal”) and Eastern Khanty сө̆ӽ (sø̆ḥ, “leather, skin”).

parole.significato: heart (a muscular organ that pumps blood through the body)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *śüdäme. Cognate with Northern Mansi сым (sym), Finnish sydän, Estonian süda and Erzya седей (sedej).
Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Uralic *śićä or *śińćä (“inside”). Cognates include Finnish sisä.

parole.significato: to find, come across, stumble upon (encounter or discover by accident)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *tole- + -ál (frequentative suffix). Cognates include Finnish tulla.

parole.significato: to teach (to pass on knowledge to)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *tuna- (“to get used to, to learn”) + -ít (causative suffix). Cognates include Moksha and Erzya тонадомс (tonadoms, “to get used to, to learn”), and Eastern Mari туныкташ (tunyktaš, “to teach”).

parole.significato: stern (the rear part or after end of a ship or vessel)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *tuktɜ, *tukta (“cross-beam”). Cognate with Finnish tuhto (“thwart (of a ship)”), Komi-Zyrian тік (tik, “cross wood, cross bar”), and Tym Southern Selkup тати (tati, “thwart (of a ship)”).
From the same Proto-Uralic root *tinä as e.g. Finnish sinä, Erzya тон (ton), Eastern Mari тый (tyj) and Komi-Zyrian тэ (te).

parole.significato: full (of something -val/-vel), normally with explicit or implied van
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *täwde. Cognates include Finnish täysi, Estonian täis.
From the same Proto-Uralic *täwde (“full”) as tele (“full”) + -es (adjective-forming suffix).

parole.significato: you guys, you all, y'all, you folks, you (second-person plural, nominative, informal form)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Uralic *te. Compare Finnish te.

parole.significato: feather (a branching, hair-like structure that grows on the bodies of birds, used for flight, swimming, protection and…
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *tulka.
From Proto-Uralic *to. Cognates include Erzya тов (tov), Finnish tuo.

parole.significato: to know (to be aware of some information)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *tumte-. Cognate with Finnish tuntea and Estonian tundma.
From Proto-Uralic *tälwä (“winter”). Cognates include Southern Mansi тӓ̄л (tǟl), Northern Mansi та̄л (tāl), Moksha тяла (täla), Erzya теле (tele), Finnish talvi and Estonian talv.
From Proto-Uralic *towe (“lake, pond”). Cognates include Southern Mansi то̄ (tō, “lake”).
Lexicalization of Proto-Uralic *to (“that”) + -l (ablative suffix).

parole.significato: lung (a biological organ that controls breathing, and oxygenates the blood), (in compound words) pulmonary
parole.testo: According to the Uralic etymological database it is from Proto-Uralic *täwe. Cognates include Finnish tävy and Komi-Zyrian ты (ty). However, it is of unknown origin in every other source. The New Etymological Dictionary of Hungarian says the Proto-Uralic explanation is wrong due to phonetic and morp

parole.significato: udder (part of domestic milk-giving animal that expresses milk)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *tuďka (“tip, peak, something protruding”). Cognates include Northern Mansi талях (talâh, “top, summit, edge”).

parole.significato: finger, toe, digit (whether on hands or feet; inclusive of the thumb)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *suwďa. Cognates include Northern Mansi туля (tulâ).
From Proto-Uralic *soja (“sleeve”).

parole.significato: crow (a bird of the genus Corvus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *warᴈ with Hungarian derivation. Cognate to Finnish varis. For the ending, compare borjú, gyapjú.
From Proto-Uralic *waśke. Cognate with Finnish vaski.

parole.significato: to take, grab (out of some food etc.: -ból/-ből)
parole.testo: From earlier *vewə- (compare vevő ‘buying’, vett ‘he bought’), from Proto-Uralic *wexe- (“to take”). Often considered a doublet of visz (“to carry”), but this may not be correct.

parole.significato: to take, carry (optionally, some object for someone: -nak/-nek)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *wixe- (“to bring, carry”). Cognate with Northern Mansi виӈкве (viňkve), Erzya виемс (vijems), Estonian viima, Finnish viedä. Often considered a doublet of Hungarian vesz (“to buy, take”), but this may not be correct.
From Proto-Uralic *wajŋe (“spirit”). For semantic development compare lelkes. Earlier suggested as back-formation from vágyás, vágyódás.
From Proto-Uralic *wolka. Compare Finnish olka.
From Proto-Uralic *were. Cognates include Northern Mansi вы̄гыр (vȳgyr), Finnish veri and Estonian veri.
From Proto-Uralic *woje-.
From Proto-Uralic *wete. First attested in the late 12th century. Cognates include Northern Mansi вит (vit), Erzya ведь (veď), Finnish vesi, Estonian vesi.

parole.significato: grebe (aquatic diving bird in the order Podicipediformes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *wajće (“duck”) + -k (noun-forming suffix). First attested in 1519.
From Proto-Uralic *waδ’kɜ (“small river”). First attested in 1009.
From Proto-Uralic *wäŋew. Cognates include Finnish vävy. (Probably not related to vőlegény (“fiancé, bridegroom”).)

parole.significato: sister-in-law (the wife of a usually close, older male relative, such as a brother or an uncle)
parole.testo: Possibly derived from Proto-Uralic *ańa (“wife of an older male relative; mother”).

parole.significato: through, across, over (from one place to another)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic.
From Proto-Uralic *ipsɜ or *ipśɜ (“smell, taste”), the same root as the noun íz (“taste”) + -es (adjective-forming suffix), hence a doublet of ízes.
From Proto-Uralic *üje. Cognate with Finnish yö, Estonian öö.

parole.significato: to live (to remain alive, be alive, sometimes to reside at)
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *elä-. Cognates include Finnish elää (“to live”).

From Old Hungarian ɛ̄n. Usually considered to continue the Proto-Uralic first-person pronoun *minä (compare e.g. Finnish minä), but there is no consensus on how the Hungarian word has developed to its present shape. At least four proposals have been advanced: * irregular loss of the word-initial *m-
From Proto-Uralic *särä. Cognates include Northern Mansi та̄р (tār, “root”).
Controversial origin: * From ér (“blood vessel”). * From Proto-Uralic *šerɜ (“creek”).
From Proto-Uralic *joŋse. Cognates include Northern Mansi ё̄вт (jōvt), Finnish jousi. Doublet of ív (“arc”).
From Proto-Uralic *sëne (“sinew”). Cognates include Northern Mansi та̄н (tān), Finnish suoni and Estonian soon, Erzya сан (san).
From Proto-Uralic *jëŋse or *joŋse (“bow”). Doublet of íj (“bow”).
Possibly from Proto-Uralic *ipse, if only í-reflects the original root and z- is an obscured suffix. Cognates include Northern Mansi ат (at).

From Proto-Uralic *oma (“old, previous”). Cognate with Finnish ammoin (“very long ago”), Estonian ammu (“once upon a time, long ago”), Northern Sami oames (“past, old”), and Erzya умок (umok, “a long time ago”). Compare agg (“aged”), avas (“rancid”), avul (“to become obsolete”), avítt (“antiquated”)
From Proto-Uralic *wolnɜ (“tin”).
From Proto-Uralic *wᴕjɜ-.
From Proto-Uralic *süle. Cognates include Finnish syli.
Possibly from Proto-Uralic *weńćɜ ~ *wećɜ (“every, all, whole”). Compare Erzya весе (vese, “every, all”).

From Proto-Uralic *witte. Cognates include Northern Mansi ат (at), Northern Khanty вет (wjet), Finnish viisi, Estonian viis and Nganasan бииˮ (bīʔ, “ten”). The labialization *i > *ü > ö after original *w is regular; compare öl (“to kill”) from *widä-.

parole.significato: belt (a band worn around the waist to hold clothing to one's body (usually pants) to serve as a decorative piece of clo…
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *üwä.
From Proto-Uralic *uje- (“swim”) + -sz ([now obsolete] frequentative suffix) + -ik. Cognates include Finnish uida, Estonian ujuma, Northern Mansi уйгалаӈкве (ujgalaňkve), Southern Khanty [Term?].
First attested in 1055 in the establishing charter of the abbey of Tihany. From Proto-Uralic *utka. Cognate with Tundra Nenets ӈуˮ (ŋù', “track”).

parole.significato: ancient, very old; mostly used in compounds as a prefix; otherwise poetic
parole.testo: From Proto-Uralic *ićä (“father”). Cognates include Finnish isä, Estonian isa, Moksha оця (ocä) and Northern Sami áhčči.

parole.significato: roe deer (a small deer species of Europe, Asia Minor, and Caspian coastal regions, Capreolus capreolus)
parole.testo: Thought to be of unknown origin earlier, but possibly from Proto-Uralic *wetɜ. Compare Estonian vedis, Livonian vediks, Erzya ведяка (veďaka) and Moksha [script needed] (vedraš).
